references.text: The Lord commanded that all the firstborn among the children of Israel should be consecrated to Him, which forms the basis for the counting of the firstborn in Numbers 3:40.
The law concerning the redemption of the firstborn is given here, and this count in Numbers serves to determine the number of firstborn who must be redeemed.
The explanation for why the firstborn belong to the Lord—linked to the killing of the firstborn in Egypt—provides the background for the counting.
The Lord declares that the Levites are to be taken in place of all the firstborn among the children of Israel, which explains the purpose of this count.
Moses carries out the Lord's command and counts the firstborn, with the result that there were 22,273 firstborn.
The law concerning the redemption of the firstborn is repeated, specifying that they are to be redeemed from one month old, the same age limit as in the count.
The reference to the law that every male firstborn shall be called holy to the Lord shows the continuity of this arrangement into the New Testament.
